sections.html:
Speed in Glendale comes from one of two choices. Take a cash offer on the house in its present state, or make repairs and list for a buyer who needs a loan. Skipping prep saves weeks. A repaired listing can fetch more, but only if the house shows well and months of waiting are acceptable.

  • Cash as-is: inherited houses, deferred repairs, properties with tenants, and sellers facing a move or a payment deadline.
  • Agent listing: a house that shows well, with an owner willing to host open houses and endure an inspection period.
  • Sale by owner: sellers who are comfortable pricing, writing contracts and filling out disclosure forms alone.

Glendale is a Maricopa County city about nine miles northwest of downtown Phoenix. Its 260,572 residents (July 1, 2025) are up 4.9% on the 248,371 of the April 2020 estimates base, and the city covers 61.6 square miles. The New River and the Agua Fria River run along its western edge.

Renters are a big part of this market, since owners occupy only 57.2% of homes. Median value of an owner-occupied house is $387,500, rent is $1,528 at the median, and 88,633 households average 2.80 people. Workers spend 27.7 minutes getting to work on average.

Neighborhoods vary. The original 1895 townsite, bounded by Lamar Road, 55th Avenue, Myrtle Avenue and 59th Avenue, holds the oldest streets. Arrowhead Ranch, around Arrowhead Towne Center, grew later as a hub for housing and shopping. Values and repair needs can differ between the two, so price against sales close to your own block.

Tenants in the house? Look at the county registration first. A.R.S. 33-1902 bars occupancy of a residential rental unless the Maricopa County Assessor holds the owner's name, address and phone, the parcel number and the year built. Report any change within ten days. Owners living outside Arizona add an in-state statutory agent.

Registration problemWhat can happen
Tenant of an unregistered property sends a ten day written noticeIf the owner does not file in time, the tenant may end the lease and recover prepaid rent
Property acquired after the last valuation noticesThe city or town assesses a $1,000 civil penalty plus $100 for each further month
Other noncomplianceA city or town may impose up to $150 per day, and a court dismisses the case if the owner files within ten days of the complaint

Landlords got a tax break on January 1, 2025: long-term residential rentals of 30 days or more no longer carry city transaction privilege tax reporting or payment. The county registration duty stays. Questions about older tax periods go to the Business Licensing Office, (623) 930-3190 or taxlic@glendaleaz.com.

Short-term rental owners must register and name an emergency contact. City Code Section 29.1-41 asks vacation and short-term rental owners for the name and phone details of someone who handles complaints. The term covers any residential property offered for fewer than 30 days.

The state adds its own step: a transaction privilege tax license from the Arizona Department of Revenue. With the transient tax included, the city reports a combined rate of 15.7%. A nuisance parties and unlawful gatherings ordinance also makes owners responsible for repeated disturbances at any private residence, whether rented short term, rented long term or owner-occupied.

State law, A.R.S. 9-500.39, bars an outright ban. Cities may still set safety rules and zoning, charge permit fees up to $250, and fine up to $3,500, or three nights' rent if higher, for a third violation in one year.

Glendale's Building Safety Division reviews plans electronically. A homeowner, an architect or a contractor with an Arizona Registrar of Contractors license may apply, and contractors also need a Glendale business license. Owners who do the work themselves sign a statement to that effect.

Deadlines matter when a seller is finishing a project. A permit stays active only if work starts within 180 days of issuance and one inspection passes in every 180 day period, up to a two year maximum. An extension of a live permit costs half the original fee, 50 percent, but reviving an expired one costs the full fee and may need new plans if the code has changed. Changing the size of a window opening can call for a larger structural header.

Did an earlier owner add a patio cover, room or garage conversion? Ask Development Services if that permit was finaled, because inspectors and lenders raise the question too.

Your Glendale bill comes from Maricopa County and is paid in two halves, October 1 and March 1. Late status begins at 5:00 p.m. on November 1 for the first half, shifting to the next business day when that is a weekend, and after May 1 for the second, under A.R.S. 42-18052.

To contest a valuation, start with the Assessor. A Notice of Value arrives between January 1 and March 1, and you have 60 days from the mailing date to file a petition for review. A.R.S. 42-16051 wants your opinion of full cash value plus support, for instance the sale price of a comparable property. A denial moves the case to the State Board of Equalization, and the county sets December 15 as the court filing date. Because Arizona taxes the limited property value, which climbs at most 5% a year, a lower full cash value only helps if it drops under the limited value.

Glendale deeds are filed with the Maricopa County Recorder, an office that manages more than 52 million documents. Its staff point form questions to a title company or attorney. An affidavit of value goes with the deed under A.R.S. 11-1133, and gifts and certain family transfers are exempt under A.R.S. 11-1134.

sections.h2: From offer to closing in Glendale
sections.html:
Saying yes to an offer starts escrow at a title company. The officer searches for liens, requests your mortgage payoff, apportions property tax and drafts the deed and affidavit. Cash buyers bring no lender, so nothing waits on loan approval or an appraisal. Financed buyers need both, and an unfinished permit or unregistered rental can slow that file.

With tenants in place, disclose the lease at the outset and collect the registration record, rent roll and deposit details. For an inherited house, give the title officer the paperwork on who now owns it. Do these steps before the offer arrives, and closing runs on its own schedule instead of a scramble.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a Glendale rental with the county before selling it?
faqs.a: Yes, if tenants live there. Arizona law requires the owner of residential rental property to keep registration details on file with the county assessor and to update them within ten days of a change. Without that filing, a tenant can end the lease and recover prepaid rent.

faqs.q: Does Glendale charge city tax on long-term rental income?
faqs.a: No, not since January 1, 2025. Owners of residential rentals of 30 days or more no longer report or remit city transaction privilege tax on that income, though the property must still be registered with the county assessor.

faqs.q: What rules apply to a short-term rental in Glendale?
faqs.a: The owner gives the city emergency and complaint contacts under City Code Section 29.1-41, holds a state transaction privilege tax license, and collects tax at a combined rate the city reports as 15.7%. A short-term rental is a residential property rented for fewer than 30 days.

faqs.q: When do Glendale property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: The first half turns delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and the second half after 5:00 p.m. on May 1. When November 1 falls on a weekend, the county moves the first-half date to the next business day.

faqs.q: How long does a Glendale building permit stay active?
faqs.a: A permit expires if work does not begin within 180 days, and one passed inspection is needed in every 180 day period. The project has a two year maximum, and an extension of an unexpired permit costs 50 percent of the original fee.
